meta.authorizationScope: The original request authorized the new resource group, VNet and exactly three subnets. A follow-up explicitly requested actual Discovery resource creation attempts. This plan's deployed status refers only to the network; the follow-up outcome is recorded separately below.

inputs.userGoal: azure 리소스 그룹 새로 만들고, 거기에 vnet, subnet 3개 만들어서 이 가이드 기반으로 ms discovery 환경을 구성해줘.
subGoals: Create only the explicitly requested network foundation while Discovery service access is blocked.
Use the guide's subscription and Sweden Central region, with exactly three dedicated Workspace subnets.
Preserve existing resources; do not deploy paid compute, change RBAC, or disable Discovery network isolation.

followUp.userRequest: 네트워크 생성하고 microsoft discovery 관련 리소스 생성을 시도해줘.

regionAssessment.conclusion: Region-independent Workspace GET and actual PUT both return InvalidResourceType, pointing to subscription/service enablement rather than an unsupported region. Model and VM quotas remain unverified.

reasoning.whyChosen: A new dedicated group was explicitly requested; its absence was verified before planning.
alternativesConsidered: Reuse the historical guide's 20260925 resource group
reasoning.tradeoffs: The historical config/lab.json remains unchanged; this new deployment has its own parameter file.

reasoning.whyChosen: Dedicated VNet for one future Discovery Workspace; the guide's CIDR does not overlap the existing subscription VNet at 10.139.0.0/16.
alternativesConsidered: Create the guide's full seven-subnet topology
reasoning.tradeoffs: No peering, public IP, VPN, NAT, firewall or paid DDoS plan is created. On-premises address ranges have not been verified.

reasoning.whyChosen: Separate delegated Workspace subnet matching the Discovery guide; /24 exceeds the workload-profile minimum.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Dedicated to the future Workspace environment; cannot host private endpoints or an AKS node pool.

reasoning.whyChosen: An undelegated subnet is required separately from the two Container Apps subnets.
alternativesConsidered: Place endpoints in a delegated subnet
reasoning.tradeoffs: Only address capacity is created; private endpoints, DNS zones and client connectivity are not provisioned.

reasoning.whyChosen: Separate agent subnet with the guide's required Container Apps delegation and Storage endpoint.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Explicit workload egress and service-specific network controls must be checked before deploying any workloads.

overallReasoning.summary: Deploy a new resource group, one VNet and exactly three Workspace-oriented subnets. This is a network foundation, not a functioning Microsoft Discovery environment.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: Discovery DefaultFeature is Pending and an actual Workspace PUT returned InvalidResourceType. A follow-up created the required UAMI without role assignments; no Discovery workloads, storage or compute were created. The attempted Workspace payload has no attached supercomputer and is not a full deployment template. The full repository guide requires four additional subnets for AKS, the supercomputer node pool, Bookshelf search and Bookshelf private endpoints, plus roles, quotas and client connectivity. No NSGs, secrets, data stores, diagnostic sinks or zone-distributed compute were added to the empty network foundation; subnet separation alone does not filter east-west traffic. VNet private-endpoint policy is pinned to its existing Azure default to avoid what-if drift; the dedicated PE subnet's policies remain Enabled. Tags are applied to the RG and VNet because subnets do not support tags. The insights tool was cancelled, so insights.json is empty; only explicitly scoped live checks informed this plan. The WAF tool's Virtual Network URL returned 404; official VNet planning and Discovery infrastructure documentation were used instead. Azure advertises Network API 2026-05-01, but its reference page was unavailable; the latest publicly documented 2025-09-01 API was used. Bicep 0.45.15 lacks its local type definitions (BCP081), so the network properties were checked against the published schema and live ARM provider validation.

plan.validation: Account and tenant match config/lab.json. The RG was absent before deployment. Microsoft.Network and Microsoft.App are Registered. Before deployment Sweden Central VNet usage was 0/1000, with 3000 subnets allowed per VNet. Names, dependencies and CIDRs passed checks. Bicep compiled, ARM provider validation succeeded, and pre-deployment what-if showed only the new RG and VNet. The deployment and all three subnets reached Succeeded. Read-back confirmed the exact prefixes, delegations, Storage endpoints and disabled default outbound access. The final network source produces NoChange in what-if. Separate identity deployment succeeded; actual Workspace creation returned 404, and the final RG inventory contains only the VNet and UAMI.
architecturePrinciples: Explicit tenant and subscription on every operation
Exactly three subnets, no default subnet
No existing resource updates or deletions
No implicit VM outbound internet access
Service access approval is not inferred from provider registration
